issues.title: Wayfinder: In-app notifications for Cadence
issues.body:
## Destination

A spec (PRD issue) for production-grade Notifications in Cadence, delivered through one hosted third-party vendor. It covers the vendor, the notification catalogue across all four roles, user preferences, and how the Notification Feed looks and behaves in the app. v1 is Notification Feed only: no email, no web push.

## Notes

- Domain: Cadence app (`app/`). Use the language in `GLOSSARY.md`: **Notification** and **Notification Feed** were added for this effort, and the recipients are Student, Instructor, Platform Admin and Team Admin.
- Production grade: real per-user security against the vendor (signed user tokens etc.). It must still work with whichever user the DevUI switcher selects.
- Hosted vendor only. Never self-host.
- The vendor must have a free tier usable in development. We build the Notification Feed UI ourselves, so the vendor's React components don't matter, but a headless feed API does.
- Sign up for as few services as possible: pick one sensible vendor, then prototype against it. No bake-off.
- There's no mobile app, so "push" means browser web push.
- Leave room for email: nothing in v1 may shut out a later email step. Preferences are category × channel, with only `in_app_feed` used for now.
- **Vendor behind Cadence-owned interfaces.** Only adapters touch Knock. There's a server interface (triggering, preferences, user sync) and a client interface (feed list, counts, mark seen/read, live updates), both in Cadence's language; the adapters map to Knock keys. Swapping vendors means writing new adapters. Set by [How do Notification preferences work in Cadence?](https://github.com/ai-hero-dev/cohort-005-project/issues/20#issuecomment-6059881412)
- Default skills for grilling tickets: `grilling` + `domain-modeling`.

## Decisions so far

<!-- the index: one line per closed ticket, enough to judge relevance, then zoom the link for the detail the ticket holds -->
- [Which hosted notification vendor fits Cadence?](https://github.com/ai-hero-dev/cohort-005-project/issues/13): Knock — free 10K msgs/mo, mandatory RS256 signed user tokens, category × channel prefs, headless feed API; web push via FCM, paid tier jumps to $250/mo
- [How far can web push reach without a native app?](https://github.com/ai-hero-dev/cohort-005-project/issues/14): Email is the default out-of-app channel; web push is an extra opt-in channel only (iOS needs a Home Screen web app install, prompts need a user gesture, delivery is best-effort); MagicBell and SuprSend support it natively
- [Which Notifications does Cadence send, and to whom?](https://github.com/ai-hero-dev/cohort-005-project/issues/15): 7 Notifications in v1, all caused by someone else: Refund Request approved/declined → buyer; new Open Refund Request → all Platform Admins; Claimed Seat → Team Admin; new Enrollment → Instructor (off by default, opt-in); Discussion Question → Instructor; Discussion Reply → question author. No ratings, new lessons or edits. *Amended by the channels ticket:* an 8th, Refund Request confirmation → buyer
- [Pick the notification vendor](https://github.com/ai-hero-dev/cohort-005-project/issues/16): Knock, provisional until the Knock prototype passes; Courier is the fallback; Firebase/email-provider sign-ups wait on the channel decision; $250/mo cliff accepted
- [Sign up for the notification vendor and provision dev keys](https://github.com/ai-hero-dev/cohort-005-project/issues/17): Knock Development env provisioned. `KNOCK_PUBLIC_API_KEY`, `KNOCK_SECRET_API_KEY`, `KNOCK_SIGNING_KEY` and `KNOCK_FEED_CHANNEL_ID` are in `.env`; enhanced security is on and a signed-token feed call is verified
- [Does Knock hold up against Cadence?](https://github.com/ai-hero-dev/cohort-005-project/issues/21): Knock confirmed. All four checks pass (DevUI-switched signed tokens, SDK trigger to feed, headless feed list/counts/mark-seen-read, opt-in preference). "Off by default" must be written into each user's own preferences by Cadence; Knock's environment default is dashboard-only and the tenant default didn't work
- [Which channels does each Notification go out on?](https://github.com/ai-hero-dev/cohort-005-project/issues/18): Feed only in v1, no email or web push. Existing Postmark refund emails stay until Notification email lands. New Notification 8, Refund Request confirmation → buyer: own-action rule gains a "request awaiting someone else's decision" exception
- [What does the Notification Feed look like in Cadence?](https://github.com/ai-hero-dev/cohort-005-project/issues/19#issuecomment-6059737349): bell popover in the sidebar header, badge counts unseen; one chronological list with infinite scroll and history kept forever; real sender avatars with a category icon; a ✓ marks a row read; clicking goes to the most specific place; deleted comments' Notifications disappear
- [How do Notification preferences work in Cadence?](https://github.com/ai-hero-dev/cohort-005-project/issues/20#issuecomment-6059881412): 6 mutable categories (Refund Request updates, Open Refund Requests, Seat claims, Enrollments, Discussion Questions, Discussion Replies) × channel, feed only; Enrollments off, rest on; switches shown by what the person is or has, not role; a Notifications card on `/settings`, saves on flip by merging into the preference set; no mute-all
- [How does Cadence's Notification plumbing work against Knock?](https://github.com/ai-hero-dev/cohort-005-project/issues/22#issuecomment-6060008522): Knock only, no local store; triggers inline after commit, best-effort with idempotency keys; deleted comments archived via `trigger_data` lookup; explicit user sync writes default prefs, admins queried at trigger time; real-time socket + bulk channel status updates; fake adapter in tests, no-op in keyless dev

## Not yet specified

None. The fog is cleared, and the PRD is next.

## Out of scope

- Native mobile apps (and native mobile push)
- Self-hosting a notification vendor
- Building our own delivery infrastructure
- SMS and chat channels (Slack etc.)
- Email as a Notification channel: a follow-up effort, expected soon. The existing direct Postmark refund emails carry on until then ([Which channels does each Notification go out on?](https://github.com/ai-hero-dev/cohort-005-project/issues/18))
- Web push: a Firebase/FCM sign-up, a service worker, a permission UX and iOS install friction for best-effort delivery ([Which channels does each Notification go out on?](https://github.com/ai-hero-dev/cohort-005-project/issues/18))
- Refund payout Notifications (Pending, Issued and Failed Refunds): these wait on Cadence tracking Refund payouts, which is a separate effort. Failed Refund → buyer is the likely first one ([How does Cadence's Notification plumbing work against Knock?](https://github.com/ai-hero-dev/cohort-005-project/issues/22#issuecomment-6060008522))

issues.title: Which hosted notification vendor fits Cadence?
issues.body:
## Question

Which hosted notification vendor should Cadence use? Compare Knock, Novu Cloud, MagicBell, Courier and SuprSend (and any strong option we've missed) on:

- **Free tier usable in development** (must-have)
- A headless in-app feed API: list a user's Notifications, unread count, mark read/seen. We build the UI ourselves, so prebuilt React components don't matter.
- Triggering from a Node server (SDK or REST)
- Production-grade per-user auth for the feed (signed user tokens or similar)
- Web push and email as channels on the same workflow
- Per-user preferences stored by the vendor (per category × per channel)
- Pricing beyond the free tier

Finish with one recommended vendor and the reasons.

comments.body:
## Resolution: use **Knock**

Knock is the only candidate that meets every criterion on its free plan:

- **Free tier:** 10K messages a month on the Developer plan.
- **Feed auth:** in production it *requires* signed user tokens. These are RS256 JWTs that our server signs for whichever user is in the session, so they work with the DevUI switcher.
- **Preferences:** vendor-stored, by category × channel type.
- **Feed API:** a mature headless feed API with list, `unread_count`/`unseen_count` and mark seen/read/archived.
- **Triggering:** Node SDK.

The costs:

- **Web push goes through Firebase Cloud Messaging.** Knock has no first-party web push channel, so we need the Firebase SDK, a service worker and a Firebase project.
- **Steep jump to paid.** Starter is $250/mo for 50K messages, then $0.005 per message.

**How the others compare**

- **Novu Cloud:** has the cheapest paid tier (from $30/mo). Its feed auth is a static HMAC of the subscriber id with no expiry, and its preferences cover workflow × channel only, with no categories.
- **MagicBell:** has native VAPID web push, user JWTs and category × channel preferences. The free tier is only 1K deliveries a month, and the next tier is $249/mo.
- **Courier:** has scoped JWTs with expiry, topic × channel preferences and pay-as-you-go pricing at $0.005/send. Web push needs OneSignal or FCM. It is the runner-up.
- **SuprSend:** has native web push and ES256 JWTs, but vendor-stored preferences are not on Free and category preferences need Business at $250/mo. It fails the brief.

Full findings with sources: https://github.com/ai-hero-dev/cohort-005-project/blob/research/notification-vendors/docs/research/notification-vendors.md

issues.title: How far can web push reach without a native app?
issues.body:
## Question

Cadence has no mobile app. How far can browser web push actually reach? Cover browser and OS support (desktop and mobile), iOS/iPadOS's home-screen web app requirement, how the permission prompt works and what browsers require before showing it, service worker requirements, and how hosted notification vendors support web push. Is web push a credible channel for Cadence, or should email be the default out-of-app channel?

comments.body:
## Resolution

**Conclusion:** Email should be Cadence's default out-of-app channel. Web push is credible only as an extra channel people opt into, and everything it sends should also land in the Notification Feed.

**Key facts**
- **Desktop and Android:** supported in Chrome 42+, Edge 17+, Firefox 44+ (Android 48+), Safari 16+ on macOS Ventura+, and Samsung Internet. Android WebView has no support, so in-app browsers built on it can't subscribe.
- **iOS/iPadOS 16.4+:** web push works only after the person adds Cadence to their Home Screen as a web app (manifest with `display: standalone`/`fullscreen`). Plain Safari tabs can't receive it. For a web-only product that is a big drop-off.
- **EU:** Apple kept Home Screen web apps in iOS 17.4 after removing them in the betas. This was confirmed only through a search snapshot, so recheck it if we rely on it.
- **Permission prompts:** Firefox 72+ and Safari need a user gesture before they show the prompt. Once someone blocks the prompt, the site can't ask again. Best practice is our own soft pre-prompt first, at a moment when the benefit is obvious.
- **Chrome penalties:** a quieter permission prompt for sites with low acceptance; since Oct 2025, permission is removed automatically from sites whose notifications get little engagement (installed web apps are exempt); since Jan 2026, disruptive sites are rate-limited.
- **Technical:** HTTPS, a service worker, `PushManager.subscribe({ userVisibleOnly: true, applicationServerKey })` with VAPID keys (RFC 8292), and every push must show a visible notification. Delivery is best-effort (RFC 8030): messages can be dropped and subscriptions can expire at any time.
- **Vendors:** MagicBell (native support; it manages VAPID keys; the free plan has 1,000 deliveries a month) and SuprSend (native WebPush; the free plan has 10k notifications a month) support web push themselves. Knock, Novu and Courier only offer it through other providers such as FCM. A vendor saves the build work but doesn't get around the iOS or permission limits.

**Findings (with sources):** https://github.com/ai-hero-dev/cohort-005-project/blob/research/web-push-reach/docs/research/web-push-reach.md

issues.title: Which Notifications does Cadence send, and to whom?
issues.body:
## Question

What is the notification catalogue? For each of Student, Instructor, Platform Admin and Team Admin: which events produce a Notification, who exactly receives it, and what it says at a high level. Start from events that already exist in the code (Refund Requests and their outcomes, Refunds, Enrollments, Claimed Seats, comments, questions, ratings, new lessons) and decide which make the cut for v1.

comments.body:
## Resolution: the v1 Notification catalogue

**Rule:** a Notification is sent for an event that concerns the recipient and was caused by someone else, or by the system. Nobody gets a Notification about their own action. There are no digests, nudges, marketing messages or receipts.

| # | Event | Recipient | Says (high level) | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A Refund Request is approved | The buyer (a Student, or the Team Admin for a Team Licence) | The course and Purchase, that it was approved, and the decision note if one was given | On |
| 2 | A Refund Request is declined | The buyer | The course and Purchase, that it was declined, the decision note, and that they can ask again | On |
| 3 | A new Open Refund Request | Every Platform Admin | Who asked, which course, the amount, the reason, and a link to `admin.refunds`. When one admin decides it, the other admins' Notifications stay as they are | On |
| 4 | A Seat is claimed | The Team Admin who owns the Team Licence | Who claimed it, which course, and how many Seats are left (one per claim, no "all Seats claimed" Notification) | On |
| 5 | A new Enrollment, from an Individual Purchase or a Claimed Seat, including a Lapsed Student enrolling again. Buying a Team Licence doesn't count | The course's Instructor | Which Student, which course | **Off**. Each Instructor opts in through the general preferences mechanism, not a setting just for Instructors |
| 6 | A new Discussion Question (from anyone except the course's Instructor, Platform Admins included) | The course's Instructor | Who asked, which lesson, a snippet, and a link | On |
| 7 | A Discussion Reply from someone other than the question's author | The author of the Discussion Question only (not everyone in the thread) | Who replied, which lesson, a snippet, and a link | On |

**Not in v1:**
- Confirming a Refund Request to the person who made it (it's their own action).
- Ratings.
- New lessons: there's no lesson publish event, so it would notify Students about lessons that are still drafts.
- Edits and deletions of Discussion comments.
- Notifying everyone in a discussion thread ("follow").
- Other Platform Admin Notifications (Purchases, Instructors, course status).

**Deferred:** Notifications for Pending, Issued and Failed Refunds. These states are in the glossary but not in the code, which doesn't track payouts.

**Glossary:** added **Discussion Question** and **Discussion Reply** so they don't clash with quiz questions.

**Handed to later tickets:** whether a deleted comment's Notification disappears from the Notification Feed goes to the Notification Feed ticket. Enrollment Notifications being off by default and opt-in is a hard requirement for user preferences.

**Amended** by [Which channels does each Notification go out on?](https://github.com/ai-hero-dev/cohort-005-project/issues/18#issuecomment-6059308705): the own-action rule now has an exception for confirming a request that waits on someone else's decision, and **Refund Request confirmation → buyer** is Notification 8 (on by default). The "Not in v1" line about confirming a Refund Request no longer applies.

issues.title: Pick the notification vendor
issues.body:
## Question

Given the research, which single hosted vendor do we commit to? We'll sign up for this one only and prototype against it.

comments.body:
## Resolution: **Knock**, provisionally. A prototype decides whether we keep it

- **Vendor:** Knock. Its feed API and category × channel preferences beat Courier's, and those two shape most of the remaining tickets. Web push is now a minor opt-in channel, so MagicBell's native web push no longer tips the balance. Its 1K/mo free tier is also too tight.
- **Provisional:** we commit to Knock only after [Does Knock hold up against Cadence?](https://github.com/ai-hero-dev/cohort-005-project/issues/21) passes its four checks: signed user tokens that work with the DevUI switcher, Node SDK triggering into the feed, the headless feed API (list / unread count / mark read-seen), and an opt-in-only preference. If it fails, we reopen this choice.
- **Fallback:** Courier (the runner-up). We don't sign up unless Knock fails.
- **Extra sign-ups put off:** Firebase (Knock's web push goes through FCM) and an email provider (Resend/Postmark etc.) are signed up for only if [Which channels does each Notification go out on?](https://github.com/ai-hero-dev/cohort-005-project/issues/18) puts web push or email in v1. [Sign up for the notification vendor and provision dev keys](https://github.com/ai-hero-dev/cohort-005-project/issues/17) is Knock-only.
- **Pricing:** the $250/mo paid cliff is accepted. 10K messages a month (each channel send counts) comfortably covers the 7-Notification v1 catalogue.

issues.title: Sign up for the notification vendor and provision dev keys
issues.body:
## Question

Sign up for the chosen vendor on its free tier, create a development environment, and provision the API keys/secrets needed to trigger Notifications and authenticate the Notification Feed. Record where the credentials live (e.g. `.env` variable names) and any dashboard URLs later tickets need.

comments.body:
## Resolution: Knock Development environment is set up, and the keys are in `.env`

**What was done**
- Signed up for Knock on the free Developer plan. Everything below is in the **Development** environment.
- Created an in-app feed channel ("Cadence feed").
- Generated an application signing key (RSA 4096) for signed user tokens.
- Turned on enhanced security mode for Development.

**Where the credentials live:** the repo's gitignored `.env`. It's local only, and no CI secrets are needed.

| Variable | What it is |
|---|---|
| `KNOCK_PUBLIC_API_KEY` | Public key, `pk_test_…`. Used for client-side feed calls. |
| `KNOCK_SECRET_API_KEY` | Secret key, `sk_test_…`. Server-only; used to trigger workflows and manage users. |
| `KNOCK_SIGNING_KEY` | Private signing key, single-line base-64 PEM. The Knock SDK looks for this name by default. |
| `KNOCK_FEED_CHANNEL_ID` | UUID of the in-app feed channel. |

**Dashboard:** https://dashboard.knock.app. Keys are under Platform → API keys. Channels are under Settings → Channels and sources.

**Verified:**
- The secret key can call `GET /v1/users` (200; a bogus key gets 401).
- A server-signed RS256 token (`sub` + `exp`) reads the feed with the public key (200).
- With no token, the feed call is rejected with `missing_user_token`. With a bad token, it's rejected with `invalid_user_token`. So enhanced security is enforced in Development.

**Gotchas for later tickets**
- The base-64 signing key is about 4.4K characters. Pasting it into a terminal prompt cuts it off at 4,095 characters. Paste it into an editor instead.
- Because enhanced security is on, every client feed call needs an `X-Knock-User-Token` header. That makes the DevUI-switcher check in the prototype a real test.

issues.title: Which channels does each Notification go out on?
issues.body:
## Question

For each Notification in the catalogue, which channels does it go out on: Notification Feed only, plus web push, plus email? Is web push in v1 at all, and is email in v1 at all?

comments.body:
## Resolution: v1 is **Notification Feed only**

**Channels**
- Every Notification goes to the Notification Feed, with no exceptions.
- v1 has **no email and no web push**. Both are out of scope for this effort. Each would be its own follow-up effort, and email is expected to follow soon.
- **Constraint:** nothing in v1 may shut out a later email step. Preferences are modelled as category × channel, and only `in_app_feed` is used for now. Knock workflows must leave room for an email step.

**Refund emails move into Notifications**
- Cadence already emails the buyer directly through Postmark (`app/lib/refunds.server.ts`, `app/lib/mailer.server.ts`): "Refund requested" and "Refund approved/declined".
- Both events become Feed Notifications in v1.
- The direct emails **stay alongside them** until Notifications get an email channel. Then both are replaced by Notification email together. A buyer must never lose the email about their money in the meantime.

**Change to the catalogue** (it amends [Which Notifications does Cadence send, and to whom?](https://github.com/ai-hero-dev/cohort-005-project/issues/15))
- **The rule changes.** A person doesn't get a Notification about their own action, *unless* it confirms a request they made that now waits on someone else's decision. Today only Refund Requests fit, so this still keeps out Purchase receipts, your own comments, and the like.
- **New Notification 8: Refund Request confirmation.** It goes to the buyer (a Student, or the Team Admin for a Team Licence). It names the course and the amount and says the request is under review. It is **on** by default. Whether the buyer can turn it off is for [How do Notification preferences work in Cadence?](https://github.com/ai-hero-dev/cohort-005-project/issues/20).

issues.title: What does the Notification Feed look like in Cadence?
issues.body:
## Question

How should the Notification Feed look and behave inside Cadence? Where it sits in the layout, how unread counts show, what a Notification row looks like, how read/seen works, and what clicking one does. Prototype it roughly against the real vendor, using a few Notifications from the catalogue.

comments.body:
## Resolution: a bell popover in the sidebar header with one chronological, infinitely scrolling list (variant A2)

| Aspect | Decision |
|---|---|
| **Placement** | A bell in the sidebar header, next to "Cadence". Clicking it opens a popover beside the sidebar. There's no Notifications nav item, drawer or separate page. |
| **Badge** | Counts **unseen** Notifications, shown in red and capped at "9+". Opening the popover marks them seen and the badge clears. Seen isn't read: rows stay unread until you act on them. |
| **Header** | "Notifications" on the left and a **Mark all as read** link on the right. No counts. |
| **List** | One chronological list, newest first. No Unread/Earlier sections. |
| **Row** | The sender's **real avatar** with a small category icon (Discussion, Refund, Team, Enrollment) inset at its bottom-right corner. Then a title, a one-line snippet or context, and how long ago it arrived. Unread rows have a bold title; read rows have a faded avatar. Notifications from Cadence itself, with no sender (the Refund Request confirmation), show a Cadence "C" avatar. |
| **Mark read** | Each unread row has a small ✓ that marks it read and then disappears. There's no "mark unread". |
| **Clicking a row** | Marks it read and goes to the **most specific place there is**: a Discussion Question or Reply goes to the comment itself (`#comment-…` on the lesson), not just the lesson. A Notification with nowhere to go (the Refund Request confirmation) only marks itself read, and the popover stays open. |
| **Pagination** | **Infinite scroll** inside the popover, over Knock's cursor (`after`). There are no numbered pages; Knock can't do them. |
| **History** | **Kept forever**: read Notifications stay in the list and scrolling reaches all of them. We chose this over unread-only, "the tick means done" and a 7-day recent window. |
| **Empty** | "You're all caught up." |
| **Deleted comments** | When a Discussion Question or Reply is deleted, its Notification disappears from the feed. |

### Facts found while prototyping, for later tickets
- **Avatars come from Knock.** Cadence sends `users.avatarUrl` as Knock's standard `avatar` user property. Knock looks the sender up each time the feed loads, so older Notifications pick up avatar changes. This only works if Cadence keeps Knock users in sync.
- **Pagination is by cursor:** `page_size` (100 worked) plus `after`/`before`. Paging through all 108 Notifications in the seeded test feed worked.
- **Rate limit:** about 10 quick feed reads for one user returned **429 `rate_limited`**. The prototype checks for new Notifications every 4 seconds and adds a read for every page loaded. The real build should probably use Knock's live connection.
- **"Mark all" only covers what's loaded:** opening the popover marks only the loaded items seen, and the batch "Mark all as read" marks only loaded items read. The real build needs Knock's bulk endpoints so Notifications that haven't loaded yet are covered.
- **Deleted comments:** Knock's feed leaves out archived Notifications by default, so archiving the Notification when a comment is deleted is the likely approach. Not yet tested.
- **The text is Cadence's:** each row's text is written by Cadence from the Notification's `data`, not by Knock's templates.

### Assets
- Prototype branch: `prototype/notification-feed`, shipped as a patch, [`notification-feed.patch`](https://gist.github.com/mattpocock/87be0d1df4945234bba66f775ade6768#file-notification-feed-patch). Apply it on a branch with `git am notification-feed.patch`. A2 is `InfiniteScrollPopover` in `app/components/notification-feed-prototype.tsx`. The earlier commits hold the rejected variants: the drawer, the inbox page with live toasts, Load more, and Latest + See all.

issues.title: How do Notification preferences work in Cadence?
issues.body:
## Question

How can a person control which Notifications they get, and on which channel? Settle three things:

- What they can mute: each catalogue entry, groups of entries, or each entry on each channel.
- What the defaults are for each role.
- Where the setting lives in the app (`settings.tsx`?).

The decision must support the Enrollment Notification for Instructors: it's off by default and each Instructor can opt in (see [Which Notifications does Cadence send, and to whom?](https://github.com/ai-hero-dev/cohort-005-project/issues/15)). Use the vendor's own preference model where it covers this, rather than building our own.

comments.body: Context from [Does Knock hold up against Cadence?](https://github.com/ai-hero-dev/cohort-005-project/issues/21#issuecomment-6058152223): Knock's preference model handles the Enrollment opt-in, but **Cadence has to set the default itself**. Write `enrollment` → `in_app_feed: false` into each Instructor's own `default` preference set. Knock's environment default can only be set in the dashboard (no API, a separate copy per environment), and a tenant default didn't suppress delivery when we tried it. Also, `setPreferences` replaces the whole set by default.

## Resolution: six mutable categories on a Notifications card in `/settings`, behind a Cadence-owned interface

### What a person can mute
Six **preference categories**. Each one is a Knock category, and Notifications that mean the same thing to the recipient share one:

| Category | Notifications (catalogue #) | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Refund Request updates | confirmation (8), approved (1), declined (2) | On |
| Open Refund Requests | 3 | On |
| Seat claims | 4 | On |
| Enrollments | 5 | **Off** (opt-in) |
| Discussion Questions | 6 | On |
| Discussion Replies | 7 | On |

- Preferences are stored as **category × channel**, and only the feed channel is used in v1. Adding email later means adding a channel, with no migration.
- Every category can be muted, including Refund Request decisions and Open Refund Requests. They're all Notification Feed only, and each one has a page in the app behind it (e.g. `admin.refunds`).
- No global "mute all" in v1.

### Who sees which switch
Switches depend on what the person **is or has**, not their `UserRole`. The code lets any role make a Purchase, raise a Refund Request, buy a Team Licence (and so become its Team Admin) and claim a Seat.

- Refund Request updates: they have at least one Purchase.
- Seat claims: they're a Team Admin on at least one Team Licence.
- Enrollments, Discussion Questions: they're an Instructor.
- Open Refund Requests: they're a Platform Admin.
- Discussion Replies: everyone.

A switch that isn't shown keeps its default, so it can appear later (e.g. after a first Purchase) without anything having to be written.

### Defaults
All on except Enrollments. *How* the defaults get into each user's Knock `default` preference set (Knock has no environment default via the API) stays in the map's **User sync** fog.

### Where it lives and how it saves
- A new **Notifications** card on `/settings` (`app/routes/settings.tsx`), below Profile, with one switch per row and no channel column. The Notification Feed's bell popover links to it with a gear icon.
- Each switch saves when flipped, optimistically, with a toast if the save fails. The save goes through a Cadence action that **merges** the change into the user's preference set (`setPreferences` replaces the whole set by default).

### Standing rule: vendor behind Cadence-owned interfaces
No code outside an adapter touches Knock directly. There are two interfaces, both in Cadence's language (`enrollments`, the `feed` channel, etc.), and each adapter maps those names to Knock's category and channel keys:
- **Server:** triggering, preferences, user sync.
- **Client:** the browser still talks straight to the vendor (signed token, live connection), but the feed components only call a Cadence-shaped client interface (`listNotifications`, counts, `markRead`, `subscribe`…).

Swapping vendors then means writing new adapters. vitest can use a fake adapter.

issues.title: Does Knock hold up against Cadence?
issues.body:
## Question

Does Knock hold up against Cadence? Knock is our provisional vendor (see [Pick the notification vendor](https://github.com/ai-hero-dev/cohort-005-project/issues/16)). Spike it against the real app, and confirm it only if all four checks pass:

1. **Signed user tokens:** our server signs an RS256 user token for whichever user the DevUI switcher selects, and the feed authenticates with it. Switching users switches the feed.
2. **Triggering:** the Node SDK triggers one real catalogue Notification (e.g. Discussion Reply → question author), and it shows up in that user's feed.
3. **Headless feed API:** it covers listing items, the unread count, and marking items read/seen.
4. **Preferences:** category × channel preferences can express an entry that is off by default and opt-in (new Enrollment → Instructor).

If any check fails, reopen the vendor choice and fall back to **Courier**. This is about vendor fit, not the Feed's look; that belongs to [What does the Notification Feed look like in Cadence?](https://github.com/ai-hero-dev/cohort-005-project/issues/19).

comments.body:
## Resolution: **Knock passes. We commit to it.** "Off by default" is set by Cadence, not by a Knock setting.

All four checks pass against the real app and the Knock Development environment. Courier isn't needed.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| 1. Signed user tokens | **Pass.** The server signs an RS256 token (`signUserToken`, `sub` = Cadence user id) for whichever user the DevUI selects. The browser reads that user's feed with only the public key and the token, so switching users switches the feed. A token for one user gets **403** on another user's feed. |
| 2. Triggering | **Pass.** `knock.workflows.trigger("discussion-reply", …)` from the Node SDK puts the Discussion Reply in the question author's feed within a few seconds. Passing the recipient inline (`{ id, name, email }`) creates or updates the user, so no separate sync is needed just to send. |
| 3. Headless feed API | **Pass.** `GET /v1/users/:id/feeds/:channel` returns entries plus `meta.unread_count` / `unseen_count` / `total_count`. `POST /v1/messages/batch/{seen,read,unread}` works straight from the browser (CORS is fine with the public key and user token). |
| 4. Opt-in-only preference | **Pass, with a caveat.** If a user's own preferences turn the `enrollment` category's in-app feed off, Knock creates no message at all. Opting in turns it back on and delivery resumes. *Where the default comes from* is the caveat, below. |

### The caveat: where "off by default" lives

- **Environment default preference set:** this is Knock's intended mechanism, but it can only be set in the dashboard. There's no API for it, each environment has its own copy, and workflow commits don't carry it. We couldn't find the control in the dashboard. (Rows in the "preference center" only control the preference UI; they don't set defaults.)
- **Tenant default (`knock.tenants.set` with `settings.preference_set`):** this didn't work. Messages triggered with `tenant: "cadence"` were still delivered with the default off, and we didn't find out why. Don't rely on it.
- **What works:** Cadence writes the default into each user's own `default` preference set itself (`enrollment` → `in_app_feed: false`), and opting in sets it to `true`. The prototype does this the first time an Instructor is the recipient of a new Enrollment, as a stand-in for doing it at user sync. The downside is that a user Cadence never set up would default to *on*.

### Gotchas for later tickets
- A workflow's **category only exists at runtime once the workflow is committed.** Our first `new-enrollment` runs had `categories: []`, so the category preference had nothing to match.
- Triggering a workflow that isn't committed returns a 404 ("workflow not found").
- **Seen isn't read:** marking items seen (the feed was opened) doesn't change `unread_count`. Calling `batch/*` with an empty `message_ids` returns a 422.
- Vite doesn't put non-`VITE_` `.env` values on `process.env`, so the prototype calls `process.loadEnvFile(".env")`.
- `users.setPreferences` replaces the whole preference set by default. Merge with the existing set when changing one key.

### Assets
- Prototype branch: `prototype/knock-spike`, shipped as a patch, [`knock-spike.patch`](https://gist.github.com/mattpocock/87be0d1df4945234bba66f775ade6768#file-knock-spike-patch). Apply it on a branch with `git am knock-spike.patch`. The page is `/prototype/knock` (`app/routes/prototype.knock.tsx`, `app/lib/knock-prototype.server.ts`).
- Dashboard setup wizard: `scripts/prototype-knock-wizard.sh` (in the same patch) creates the `discussion-reply` (category `discussion`) and `new-enrollment` (category `enrollment`) in-app workflows in Development. Both are committed.

issues.title: How does Cadence's Notification plumbing work against Knock?
issues.body:
## Question

How does Cadence wire Notifications to Knock? Covers the fog left on the map once every ticket closed:

- **Storage**: are Notifications kept in Cadence's own database, or only in Knock?
- **Triggering**: where each Notification fires, inline or deferred, what happens when Knock fails, and how a deleted Discussion Question or Reply removes its Notification
- **User sync**: keeping Cadence users in sync with Knock, writing default preferences, targeting all Platform Admins
- **Feed freshness**: live updates without hitting Knock's rate limit; bulk mark seen/read
- **Testing**: how vitest exercises triggering without hitting Knock

comments.body:
## Resolution

Grilled with the map's owner. Every recommendation below was accepted.

### Storage
**Knock only.** Cadence stores no Notifications. The feed reads live from Knock through the client port, and a second copy would drift.

### Triggering
- **Inline, after the domain write commits.** A failure is caught and logged and never fails the domain action. There are no retries in v1: Notifications are best-effort. This is the opposite of today's Postmark refund emails, which throw after the commit.
- **Idempotency key per domain event**, e.g. `refund-approved:<refundRequestId>`, so a retry layer added later can't send duplicates.
- **Domain actions that fire Notifications move into `app/lib/*.server.ts` services** so they can be tested. This covers comment creation, Enrollment (`enrollUser`) and seat claim (`redeemCoupon`). The duplicated `createComment` in `courses.$slug.lessons.$lessonId.tsx` and `instructor.questions.tsx` becomes one function.
- **"All Platform Admins"**: at trigger time, query Cadence for every `role = admin` user and pass them as recipients. Role stays only in Cadence, so a role change needs no sync to Knock. A newly promoted admin sees only Open Refund Requests raised after the promotion.

### Deletion and edits
- When a comment is soft-deleted (`deletedAt`), archive the Notifications it caused: the Instructor's Discussion Question Notification, or the question author's Discussion Reply Notification.
- Each trigger puts the comment id in its trigger data. On delete, the server adapter lists the messages with the List Messages `trigger_data` filter (a flat JSON object of scalars) and archives them. If that filter doesn't work with the secret key during the build, fall back to a small comment id → Knock message id mapping table.
- Deleting a Discussion Question leaves the Discussion Reply Notifications under it in place, because those replies stay visible.
- Notifications are a **snapshot taken when they were sent**: editing a comment doesn't change them.

### User sync
- **Explicit sync at lifecycle points**: signup, a name change in `/settings`, Platform Admin edits in `admin.users.tsx`, and the seed. A one-off backfill script covers existing users.
- Sync identifies the user (name, email, avatar) and writes the default preference set **only if the user has none yet**. That means Enrollments off and everything else on, because Knock's environment default is dashboard-only.
- Role isn't synced. A failed sync is caught and logged, the same as a failed trigger.

### Feed freshness
- **Knock's real-time socket** (`@knocklabs/client` `listenForUpdates`, which joins the `feeds:<channel>:<user>` topic). One connection per signed-in user, in the client adapter. It feeds the bell badge and the open popover, and nothing polls.
- **The socket is torn down and re-authenticated** with a fresh signed token when the DevUI user switches.
- **Mark-seen on popover open and "Mark all as read"** use the client's bulk-by-channel status update (`bulkUpdateAllStatusesInChannel`), which runs on the user token. That covers Notifications that haven't loaded yet.

### Testing
- **The server port mirrors `MailTransport`.** It has a Knock adapter and an in-memory fake adapter that records triggers, syncs, preference writes and archives. Services take the port as an injected parameter, like `db` and `now`. No vitest test hits Knock.
- **Local dev without `KNOCK_SECRET_API_KEY`** falls back to a no-op adapter that logs, and the feed shows its empty state. This matches the `.outbox` fallback.

### Scope changes from this session
- Refund payout Notifications (Pending, Issued and Failed Refunds) are **out of scope**: they wait on Cadence tracking payouts, which is a separate effort.
- Writing the PRD isn't a ticket. The map's owner will write it from the closed tickets.

issues.title: PRD: In-app Notifications for Cadence
issues.body:
## Problem Statement

People in Cadence can't tell when something that concerns them has happened. To find out, they have to go and look:

- A Student who raised a Refund Request keeps checking back to see whether a Platform Admin has decided it.
- Platform Admins only find a new Open Refund Request by visiting the refunds admin page.
- A Team Admin can't tell when someone claims a Seat, or how many Seats are left.
- An Instructor misses Discussion Questions on their lessons.
- A Student who asked a Discussion Question doesn't know when someone replies.

Today the only out-of-app signal is the pair of direct Postmark refund emails. Cadence has nowhere inside the app to tell someone what's happened.

## Solution

Cadence gets a **Notification Feed**: a bell in the sidebar header that opens a popover listing a person's **Notifications**, newest first.

- **Badge:** counts unseen Notifications and clears when the popover opens.
- **Rows:** each row shows who caused the Notification, what happened and when. Clicking a row marks it read and goes to the most specific place in the app it's about.
- **Live updates:** new Notifications arrive without a page reload.
- **History:** kept forever and reachable by infinite scroll.

In v1 the feed is the only channel. It carries 8 Notifications across the four recipient roles: Student, Instructor, Platform Admin and Team Admin.

Each person controls which **categories** they receive from a new Notifications card on `/settings`. Enrollment Notifications are off by default and opt-in; every other category is on.

Delivery, storage and real-time updates come from one hosted vendor, **Knock**, through signed per-user tokens. The switcher in the DevUI panel keeps working: switching user switches the feed. Only Cadence-owned adapters touch Knock, so the vendor can be swapped later and an email channel can be added without a migration.

## User Stories

### Notification Feed

1. As any signed-in person, I want a bell in the sidebar header next to "Cadence", so that I can always reach my Notifications.
2. As any signed-in person, I want the bell to show a red badge with the number of unseen Notifications, so that I know at a glance that something new has happened.
3. As any signed-in person, I want the badge capped at "9+", so that a big backlog doesn't break the layout.
4. As any signed-in person, I want opening the popover to mark all my Notifications seen and clear the badge, including ones that haven't loaded yet, so that the badge only counts what I haven't looked at.
5. As any signed-in person, I want seen and read to be different things, so that opening the popover doesn't hide what I still need to act on.
6. As any signed-in person, I want one chronological list with the newest first, so that I can read what happened in order.
7. As any signed-in person, I want each row to show the real avatar of the person who caused it, with a small category icon (Discussion, Refund, Team, Enrollment) inset at the corner, so that I can see who it's from and what it's about.
8. As any signed-in person, I want each row to show a title, a one-line snippet or context, and how long ago it arrived, so that I can understand it without clicking.
9. As any signed-in person, I want unread rows to have a bold title and read rows a faded avatar, so that I can tell them apart.
10. As any signed-in person, I want Notifications from Cadence itself, with no sender, to show a Cadence "C" avatar, so that every row has a clear source.
11. As any signed-in person, I want a ✓ on each unread row that marks just that row read, so that I can clear items without leaving the popover.
12. As any signed-in person, I want a "Mark all as read" link in the popover header that also covers Notifications that haven't loaded yet, so that I can clear everything in one go.
13. As any signed-in person, I want clicking a row to mark it read and take me to the most specific place there is, so that I land right where I need to act.
14. As any signed-in person, I want clicking a Notification that has nowhere to go to only mark it read and keep the popover open, so that nothing unexpected happens.
15. As any signed-in person, I want the list to load more as I scroll, so that I can reach my whole history.
16. As any signed-in person, I want read Notifications to stay in the list for good, so that I can find something I've already dealt with.
17. As any signed-in person, I want to see "You're all caught up." when I have no Notifications, so that an empty list doesn't look broken.
18. As any signed-in person, I want new Notifications to appear in the badge and the open popover live, without reloading, so that the feed is always current.
19. As any signed-in person, I want a gear icon in the popover that links to my Notification preferences, so that I can change what I receive.
20. As any signed-in person, I want only ever to see my own Notifications, enforced by a signed token, so that nobody can read someone else's feed.

### Refund Requests

21. As a buyer (a Student, or a Team Admin for a Team Licence), I want a Notification confirming that my Refund Request is under review, naming the course and the amount, so that I know it went through.
22. As a buyer, I want a Notification when my Refund Request is approved, naming the course and Purchase and including the decision note if there is one, so that I know my money is coming back.
23. As a buyer, I want a Notification when my Refund Request is declined, with the decision note and a reminder that I can ask again, so that I know where I stand.
24. As a buyer, I want to keep getting the direct refund emails alongside these Notifications, so that I never lose the email about my money.
25. As a Platform Admin, I want a Notification for every new Open Refund Request, showing who asked, for which course, the amount and the reason, and linking to the refunds admin page, so that I can decide it promptly.
26. As a Platform Admin, I want my Open Refund Request Notification to stay as it is when another Platform Admin decides that request, so that the feed stays a faithful record.
27. As a newly promoted Platform Admin, I want Open Refund Request Notifications from my promotion onwards, so that I share the workload from then on.

### Team Licences

28. As a Team Admin, I want a Notification each time a Student claims a Seat on my Team Licence, showing who claimed it, for which course, and how many Seats are left, so that I can keep track of my licence.

### Enrollments

29. As an Instructor, I want to opt in to a Notification for every new Enrollment on my courses, whether from an Individual Purchase or a Claimed Seat, so that I can follow who joins.
30. As an Instructor, I want Enrollment Notifications off until I turn them on, so that a popular course doesn't flood my feed.
31. As an Instructor, I want a Lapsed Student enrolling again to count as a new Enrollment, so that I see them come back.
32. As an Instructor, I don't want an Enrollment Notification when a Team Licence is bought, so that I'm only told about real Students joining.

### Discussions

33. As an Instructor, I want a Notification for every new Discussion Question on my course's lessons, including ones from Platform Admins, showing who asked, which lesson and a snippet, so that I can answer it.
34. As an Instructor, I don't want a Notification for Discussion Questions I post on my own course, so that I'm not told about my own actions.
35. As the author of a Discussion Question, I want a Notification when someone else replies, showing who replied, which lesson and a snippet, so that I can follow the answer.
36. As the author of a Discussion Question, I don't want a Notification for my own replies to it, so that my feed only shows other people's activity.
37. As anyone else in a thread, I don't want Notifications for replies to someone else's Discussion Question, so that I'm not spammed by threads I didn't start.
38. As the recipient of a Discussion Notification, I want clicking it to take me to that exact comment on the lesson, so that I don't have to hunt for it.
39. As the recipient of a Discussion Notification, I want it to disappear from my feed if the comment is deleted, so that I'm not sent to something that's gone.
40. As the author of a Discussion Reply, I want deleting the Discussion Question above it to leave Notifications about my reply in place, so that Notifications about visible replies survive.
41. As the recipient of a Discussion Notification, I want it to keep the text it had when it was sent even if the comment is edited later, so that the feed is a stable record.

### Preferences

42. As any signed-in person, I want a Notifications card on `/settings`, below Profile, with one switch per category, so that I can control what reaches my feed.
43. As any signed-in person, I want each switch to save as soon as I flip it, with a toast if the save fails, so that I don't need a save button.
44. As any signed-in person, I want to see only the switches that apply to what I am or have, not to my role, so that the card stays relevant.
45. As someone with at least one Purchase, I want a "Refund Request updates" switch covering the confirmation, approval and decline, so that I can mute them together.
46. As a Team Admin on at least one Team Licence, I want a "Seat claims" switch, so that I can mute claim Notifications.
47. As an Instructor, I want "Enrollments" (off by default) and "Discussion Questions" switches, so that I can tune my teaching Notifications.
48. As a Platform Admin, I want an "Open Refund Requests" switch, so that I can mute them if someone else is on duty.
49. As anyone, I want a "Discussion Replies" switch, so that I can mute replies to my questions.
50. As someone who gains a new capability (a first Purchase, say), I want the new switch to appear with its default already in effect, so that nothing needs setting up.
51. As any signed-in person, I want changing one switch to leave my other preferences as they are, so that saving one never resets the rest.

### Identity and sync

52. As any signed-in person, I want my name and avatar in other people's Notifications to stay current after I change them, so that people recognise me.
53. As a new user, I want my default preferences in place from signup, so that Enrollments are off and everything else is on from the start.
54. As an existing user from before this launch, I want a backfill to give me the same defaults, so that I'm treated the same as a new user.

### Developers and operators

55. As a developer, I want switching user in the DevUI panel to tear down the live feed connection and reconnect with that user's signed token, so that I can test any user's feed.
56. As a developer, I want the app to keep working without Knock keys, with Notifications logged instead of sent and an empty feed, so that I can run Cadence locally without signing up.
57. As a developer, I want vitest to run every Notification rule against an in-memory fake without touching Knock, so that tests are fast and run offline.
58. As an operator, I want a Knock failure to be logged and never fail the action that caused it, so that a refund decision, comment or Enrollment always goes through.
59. As an operator, I want each Notification to carry an idempotency key for its domain event, so that a retry layer added later can't send duplicates.
60. As a future developer, I want Knock hidden behind Cadence-owned interfaces, so that switching vendors means writing new adapters and nothing else.
61. As a future developer, I want preferences stored as category × channel, so that adding email later means adding a channel, with no migration.

## Implementation Decisions

### Vendor and storage
- **Knock** is the vendor. It's confirmed by the spike (#21): RS256 signed user tokens, a headless feed API, category × channel preferences, and a free development tier.
- **Notifications live only in Knock.** Cadence doesn't store a copy, and there are no schema changes for Notifications themselves.
- The Development environment is already provisioned. `KNOCK_PUBLIC_API_KEY`, `KNOCK_SECRET_API_KEY`, `KNOCK_SIGNING_KEY` and `KNOCK_FEED_CHANNEL_ID` are in `.env`, and enhanced security is on.
- Vite doesn't expose `.env` variables without the `VITE_` prefix on `process.env` in dev, so the server must load them some other way. The spike called `process.loadEnvFile(".env")`.

### Notification catalogue
The rule: a Notification is about something that concerns the recipient and was caused by someone else, or by the system. The one exception is confirming a request that waits on someone else's decision.

| # | Event | Recipient | Category | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Refund Request approved | the buyer | Refund Request updates | On |
| 2 | Refund Request declined | the buyer | Refund Request updates | On |
| 3 | New Open Refund Request | every Platform Admin (`role = admin`) at trigger time | Open Refund Requests | On |
| 4 | Seat claimed | the Team Admin who owns the Team Licence | Seat claims | On |
| 5 | New Enrollment (Individual Purchase or Claimed Seat, including a Lapsed Student re-enrolling; not buying a Team Licence) | the course's Instructor | Enrollments | **Off** |
| 6 | New Discussion Question, from anyone except the course's Instructor | the course's Instructor | Discussion Questions | On |
| 7 | Discussion Reply from someone other than the question's author | the question's author only | Discussion Replies | On |
| 8 | Refund Request confirmation (under review) | the buyer | Refund Request updates | On |

- Each Notification is its own Knock workflow, assigned to its category. A workflow must be **committed** in Knock before its category exists at runtime, and triggering an uncommitted workflow returns 404.
- Each workflow keeps room for a later email step.
- **The text is Cadence's.** Each trigger sends structured data: names, course, lesson, snippet, amount, note, Seats left, link target and comment id. The client writes each row's title and snippet from that data. Knock templates aren't used for text.

### Server Notifications port (the seam)
- A Cadence-owned server interface, modelled on `MailTransport`, covers three things, all in Cadence's language: **triggering** a Notification, **preferences** (read, and merge a change), and **user sync** (identify, plus write default preferences if the user has none). It also covers **archiving** the Notifications caused by a comment.
- **Three adapters:**
  - **Knock:** the only code that imports the Knock SDK or knows Knock's workflow, category and channel keys.
  - **In-memory fake:** records triggers, syncs, preference writes and archives for tests.
  - **No-op:** logs; used when `KNOCK_SECRET_API_KEY` is missing, matching the `.outbox` fallback.
- Services take the port as an injected parameter, like `db` and `now`. Routes pass in the default adapter.
- **Triggers fire inline, after the domain write commits.** A port failure is caught and logged, and never changes the domain result. v1 has no retries.
- **Idempotency key per domain event,** for example `refund-approved:<refundRequestId>`, `refund-requested:<refundRequestId>`, `seat-claimed:<seatId>`, `enrollment:<enrollmentId>` and `discussion-reply:<commentId>`.
- **The recipient is passed inline** (id, name, email, avatar), which creates or updates the Knock user as it sends.
- **The actor is passed** so the sender's avatar resolves. Notification 8 has no actor.

### Services that fire Notifications
- **Refunds** (existing service): raising a Refund Request fires #8 to the buyer and #3 to every Platform Admin. Approving fires #1 and declining fires #2. The direct Postmark refund emails carry on unchanged.
- **Enrollment** (new service, extracted from the purchase route's `enrollUser`): creates the Enrollment and fires #5 to the Instructor. The Seat claim path uses it too.
- **Seat claim** (new service, extracted from the redeem route's `redeemCoupon`): claims the Seat and fires #4 to the Team Admin with the number of Seats left. The Enrollment it grants fires #5 through the Enrollment service.
- **Comments** (new service): replaces the two duplicated `createComment` functions in the lesson route and the instructor questions route.
  - Creating a top-level comment fires #6 unless the author is the course's Instructor.
  - Creating a reply fires #7 to the question's author unless the reply is theirs.
  - Soft-deleting a comment (`deletedAt`) archives the Notifications it caused: #6 for a Discussion Question, #7 for a Discussion Reply. Archiving looks them up by the comment id in the trigger data, using Knock's List Messages `trigger_data` filter.
  - If that filter doesn't work with the secret key, the fallback is a small mapping table from comment id to Knock message id. That would be the one schema change; follow the database-migrations skill.
  - Deleting a Discussion Question leaves its Discussion Reply Notifications in place.
  - Editing a comment changes no Notification.

### Preferences
- **Six categories × channel.** Only the feed channel (Cadence's `feed`, mapped by the adapter to Knock's `in_app_feed`) is used in v1. There's no mute-all.
- **Defaults:** Enrollments off, everything else on. These are written into each user's own Knock `default` preference set by user sync, and only if the user has none yet. Knock's environment default is dashboard-only, and the tenant default didn't suppress delivery in the spike.
- **Changes merge** into the existing set, because Knock's `setPreferences` replaces the whole set by default.
- **Which switches appear** depends on what the person is or has:

  | Switch | Shown when |
  |---|---|
  | Refund Request updates | they have at least one Purchase |
  | Seat claims | they're a Team Admin on at least one Team Licence |
  | Enrollments, Discussion Questions | they're an Instructor |
  | Open Refund Requests | they're a Platform Admin |
  | Discussion Replies | always |

  A hidden switch keeps its default.
- **UI:** a Notifications card on `/settings`, below Profile, with one switch per row and no channel column. Each switch saves optimistically through a Cadence action that parses its input with zod. A failed save shows a toast.

### User sync
- Sync runs at signup, after a name change in `/settings`, after Platform Admin edits in the users admin page, and in the seed. A one-off backfill script covers existing users.
- Sync sends name, email and avatar (`users.avatarUrl` as Knock's standard `avatar`) and writes the default preferences if the user has none.
- Role isn't synced. A failed sync is caught and logged.

### Client feed port
- A Cadence-shaped client interface: list Notifications (cursor-paged), unseen count, mark one read, mark all read, mark all seen, subscribe to live updates.
- A Knock adapter backs it, built on `@knocklabs/client`. Feed components only call this interface.
- **Auth:** the server signs an RS256 user token (`sub` = Cadence user id) for the current session user, the one the DevUI panel selected, and hands it to the client with the public key. A token for one user gets 403 on another user's feed.
- **Live updates:** one real-time socket per signed-in user (`listenForUpdates`). It drives both the badge and the open popover, and nothing polls; polling hit Knock's rate limit (429) in the prototype. The socket is torn down and re-authenticated when the DevUI user changes.
- **Bulk updates:** mark-seen on popover open and "Mark all as read" use the bulk-by-channel status update, so Notifications that haven't loaded are covered. Never call the batch endpoints with an empty id list (Knock returns 422).
- **Pagination:** infinite scroll over Knock's `after` cursor.
- **No Knock keys locally:** the feed shows its empty state.

### Feed UI
- **Placement:** a bell popover in the sidebar header, variant A2 from the prototype branch [`prototype/notification-feed`](https://gist.github.com/mattpocock/87be0d1df4945234bba66f775ade6768#file-notification-feed-patch) (`InfiniteScrollPopover`). There's no nav item, drawer or separate page.
- **Header:** "Notifications" on the left; "Mark all as read" and the preferences gear on the right.
- **Rows:**
  - The sender's avatar with a category icon inset; the Cadence "C" avatar when there's no sender.
  - Title, snippet and relative time.
  - Unread rows have a bold title; read rows have a faded avatar.
  - A ✓ marks a row read and then disappears. There's no mark-unread.
- **Click targets:**

  | Notification | Goes to |
  |---|---|
  | Discussion Question or Reply | the lesson with `#comment-<id>` |
  | Open Refund Request | the refunds admin page |
  | Refund decision | the buyer's Purchase or refund page |
  | Seat claim | the team page |
  | Enrollment | the Instructor's students page for the course |
  | Refund Request confirmation | nowhere: it only marks read and the popover stays open |

## Testing Decisions

- **A good test checks external behaviour through the service's public functions.** It sets up a domain state in an in-memory database, calls the action, and asserts:
  - the domain result, and
  - what the fake Notifications adapter recorded: which Notification, which recipients, which data, which idempotency key, which archives.

  Tests don't check how the adapter builds Knock calls.
- **One seam:** the server Notifications port, with the in-memory fake injected. No vitest test hits Knock.
- **Modules tested:**
  - **Refunds service:** Notifications for raising, approving and declining; every Platform Admin gets #3 and non-admins don't. A port failure doesn't fail the domain action. Team Licence buyers are treated the same way.
  - **Enrollment service:**
    - #5 goes to the course's Instructor for an Individual Purchase and for a Claimed Seat, and when a Lapsed Student re-enrolls.
    - Buying a Team Licence doesn't fire it.
  - **Seat claim service:** #4 goes to the Team Admin with the correct number of Seats left, and the Seat claim fires #5 as well.
  - **Comments service:**
    - #6 goes to the Instructor except when they ask the question themselves; a Platform Admin's question still fires it.
    - #7 goes only to the question's author and not for their own replies.
    - Deleting a question archives #6 but leaves #7 Notifications in place; deleting a reply archives its #7.
    - Both former call sites behave the same.
  - **User sync and preferences:**
    - Default preferences are written only when the user has none.
    - A change merges into the existing set.
    - Which switches appear follows what the person is or has, not their role.
- **Prior art:**
  - `refunds.server.test.ts`: an in-memory database from `createTestDb` and `seedBaseData`, plus a fixed `NOW`.
  - `mailer.server.test.ts`: the transport-port pattern.
- **Checked manually, not in vitest:**
  - The Knock adapters, which are thin mappings already proven by the spike.
  - The client feed port and bell UI: signed tokens across DevUI switches, live updates, bulk seen and read, infinite scroll, deleted-comment archiving and click targets. These are checked against the Knock Development environment.
- Before reporting done, run `npm run typecheck` then `npm run test`.

- Email as a Notification channel. It's a follow-up effort, expected soon. The existing direct Postmark refund emails carry on until it lands, and then both get replaced together.
- Web push, along with a Firebase/FCM sign-up, a service worker and a permission UX.
- Native mobile apps and native push; SMS; chat channels such as Slack.
- Self-hosting a vendor or building our own delivery infrastructure.
- Refund payout Notifications (Pending, Issued and Failed Refunds). These wait on Cadence tracking payouts.
- Ratings, new lessons, comment edits or deletions as Notifications, following threads, and other Platform Admin Notifications (Purchases, Instructors, course status).
- Digests, nudges, marketing messages and receipts.
- A global mute-all, mark-unread, numbered pages, and a separate Notifications page.
- Retries or a job queue for failed triggers. Idempotency keys leave room for these later.
- Syncing role to Knock.

## Further Notes

- Map: #12. Decisions come from #13–#22, especially:
  - #15: catalogue
  - #18: channels
  - #19: feed
  - #20: preferences
  - #21: Knock spike
  - #22: plumbing
- Prototype branches: [`prototype/knock-spike`](https://gist.github.com/mattpocock/87be0d1df4945234bba66f775ade6768#file-knock-spike-patch) (signed tokens, triggering, preferences, a dashboard wizard for workflows) and [`prototype/notification-feed`](https://gist.github.com/mattpocock/87be0d1df4945234bba66f775ade6768#file-notification-feed-patch) (feed UI variant A2).

- Knock's free tier is 10K messages a month. The paid tier jumps to $250/mo, and that cliff has been accepted.
- A user Cadence never synced would default to Enrollments **on**. The backfill and the seed close that gap.
- Use the glossary terms throughout code and copy: Notification, Notification Feed, Discussion Question, Discussion Reply, Open Refund Request, Claimed Seat, Team Admin, Platform Admin.

issues.title: Tracer bullet: Discussion Reply Notification to the question author, end to end
issues.body:
## Parent

#23

## What to build

The first Notification, working end to end against Knock. When someone replies to a Discussion Question they didn't write, the question's author sees a Notification in a new **Notification Feed**: a bell in the sidebar header that opens a popover. The Notification arrives live, without a reload.

It cuts through every layer:

- **Server Notifications port.** A Cadence-owned interface, in Cadence's language, modelled on the mail transport port. It covers triggering, preferences, user sync and archiving; this ticket only needs triggering, but the shape should leave room for the rest. It has three adapters:
  - **Knock:** the only code that imports the Knock SDK or knows Knock's workflow, category and channel keys.
  - **In-memory fake:** records what was sent, for tests.
  - **No-op:** logs, and is used when `KNOCK_SECRET_API_KEY` is missing.

  Services take the port as an injected parameter, like `db` and `now`.
- **Trigger.**
  - The Comments service fires the Discussion Reply Notification (#7) to the question's author only, and not when the author replies to their own question.
  - It fires inline after the comment is written, with the idempotency key `discussion-reply:<commentId>`.
  - It passes the recipient and the actor inline (id, name, email, avatar), and puts the comment id, lesson and snippet in the trigger data.
  - A port failure is caught and logged and never fails creating the comment.
- **Knock workflow.** A `discussion-reply` in-app workflow in the Discussion Replies category, committed in Development. Extend the Knock dashboard wizard to create it. Workflows must leave room for a later email step.
- **Signed user token.** The server signs an RS256 token (`sub` = the Cadence user id) for the current session user, the one the DevUI panel selected, and hands it to the client with the public key.
- **Client feed port.** A Cadence-shaped client interface: list, unseen count, mark read, subscribe. Its Knock adapter is built on `@knocklabs/client`, with one real-time socket per signed-in user and no polling. Switching user in the DevUI panel tears down the socket and re-authenticates with the new user's token.
- **Bell popover.** It follows variant A2 from the [`prototype/notification-feed`](https://gist.github.com/mattpocock/87be0d1df4945234bba66f775ade6768#file-notification-feed-patch) branch:
  - A red badge counting unseen Notifications.
  - A "Notifications" header.
  - Newest-first rows: the sender's real avatar with a Discussion category icon inset, then a title and a one-line snippet written by Cadence from the trigger data, then the relative time.
  - Unread rows have a bold title; read rows have a faded avatar.
  - Clicking a row marks it read and goes to that comment on the lesson (`#comment-…`).
- **Environment.** Vite doesn't put non-`VITE_` `.env` values on `process.env`, so the Knock keys need loading some other way. The Knock spike used `process.loadEnvFile`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Replying to someone else's Discussion Question puts a Notification in the question author's Notification Feed within seconds, without a reload
- [ ] Replying to your own Discussion Question sends nothing, and nobody else in the thread is notified
- [ ] Switching user in the DevUI panel switches the feed and its live connection to that user; one user's token can't read another user's feed
- [ ] The badge counts unseen Notifications
- [ ] Clicking a row marks it read and lands on the comment itself
- [ ] A failure in the port is logged and the reply is still saved
- [ ] Without `KNOCK_SECRET_API_KEY` the app runs, Notifications are logged, and the feed is empty
- [ ] Only the adapters reference Knock
- [ ] vitest covers the Comments service's Discussion Reply rule against the fake adapter (recipient, data, idempotency key, own-reply exclusion, and failure tolerance); no test hits Knock
- [ ] The wizard creates and commits the `discussion-reply` workflow
- [ ] `npm run typecheck` and `npm run test` pass

issues.title: Notification Feed: full behaviour
issues.body:
## Parent

#23

## What to build

Finish the Notification Feed so it behaves as decided in #19.

- **Infinite scroll** inside the popover over Knock's `after` cursor. There are no numbered pages.
- **History kept forever:** read Notifications stay in the list, and scrolling reaches all of them.
- **Seen when the popover opens:** opening it marks every Notification seen, including ones not loaded yet, using the client's bulk-by-channel status update. The badge clears. Seen isn't read: rows stay unread.
- **Mark all as read:** a link on the right of the header marks every Notification read, including ones not loaded, using the bulk-by-channel update.
- **✓ on each unread row:** marks just that row read and then disappears. There's no mark-unread.
- **Badge cap:** the badge reads "9+" above nine.
- **Empty state:** "You're all caught up."
- **Cadence "C" avatar:** shown for Notifications with no sender.
- **Rows with nowhere to go:** clicking one only marks it read, and the popover stays open.

Never call Knock's batch endpoints with an empty id list, because Knock returns 422.

All of this lives behind the client feed port. Feed components never touch Knock directly.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Scrolling to the bottom of the popover loads older Notifications until the whole history has loaded
- [ ] Opening the popover clears the badge even when there are more unseen Notifications than are loaded, and unread rows stay bold
- [ ] "Mark all as read" marks every Notification read, loaded or not
- [ ] The ✓ marks one row read and disappears
- [ ] The badge shows "9+" above nine
- [ ] An empty feed shows "You're all caught up."
- [ ] A Notification with no sender shows the Cadence "C" avatar
- [ ] A Notification with no click target only marks itself read and the popover stays open
- [ ] There are no 422s from empty batch calls and no polling against Knock
- [ ] `npm run typecheck` and `npm run test` pass

issues.title: Refund Request Notifications
issues.body:
## Parent

#23

## What to build

The refunds service fires Notifications as Refund Requests are raised and decided. The buyer is a Student for an Individual Purchase, or the Team Admin for a Team Licence.

- **Refund Request confirmation (#8) → buyer**, when they raise a Refund Request. It names the course and the amount and says the request is under review. It comes from Cadence itself, so it has no sender, shows the "C" avatar, and has nowhere to click.
- **Refund Request approved (#1) → buyer.** It names the course and Purchase, includes the decision note if there is one, and links to the buyer's refund or Purchase page.
- **Refund Request declined (#2) → buyer.** It names the course and Purchase, includes the decision note, and says they can ask again.
- **Open Refund Request (#3) → every Platform Admin.** Recipients are every `role = admin` user, queried at trigger time. It shows who asked, which course, the amount and the reason, and links to the refunds admin page. When one Platform Admin decides the request, the other admins' Notifications stay as they are.

Details:
- **Triggers:** each fires after the domain write commits. Failures are caught and logged, and never fail the refund action.
- **Idempotency keys:** `refund-requested:<id>`, `refund-approved:<id>`, `refund-declined:<id>` and `refund-request-open:<id>`.
- **Categories:** #8, #1 and #2 share the Refund Request updates category; #3 is in Open Refund Requests. Add the workflows to the wizard and commit them.
- **Emails:** the existing direct Postmark refund emails carry on unchanged alongside these Notifications.

- [ ] Raising a Refund Request puts a confirmation in the buyer's feed, and an Open Refund Request Notification in every Platform Admin's feed and nobody else's
- [ ] Approving or declining puts the decision, with any note, in the buyer's feed
- [ ] This works for both an Individual Purchase and a Team Licence buyer
- [ ] Clicking the Open Refund Request Notification goes to the refunds admin page, and clicking a decision goes to the buyer's refund or Purchase page
- [ ] The Postmark refund emails are still sent
- [ ] A port failure is logged and the refund action still succeeds

issues.title: User sync and the Notifications card on /settings
issues.body:
## Parent

#23

## What to build

Cadence keeps its users in sync with Knock, and people choose which Notification categories reach their feed.

- **User sync** through the server port:
  - It sends name, email and avatar (`users.avatarUrl` as Knock's standard `avatar`).
  - It writes the default preference set **only if the user has none yet**: Enrollments off, everything else on. Knock's environment default is dashboard-only, so Cadence writes each user's own `default` set.
  - It runs at signup, after a name change on `/settings`, after Platform Admin edits on the users admin page, and in the seed. A one-off backfill script covers existing users.
  - Role isn't synced. A failed sync is caught and logged.
- **Preferences** are stored as category × channel, with only the feed channel used in v1. The adapter maps Cadence's names to Knock's category keys and `in_app_feed`.

  Changing one switch **merges** into the existing set, because Knock's `setPreferences` replaces the whole set by default.
- **A Notifications card on `/settings`**, below Profile, with one switch per category and no channel column. Which switches appear depends on what the person is or has, not their role:

  | Switch | Shown when |
  |---|---|
  | Refund Request updates | they have at least one Purchase |
  | Seat claims | they're a Team Admin on at least one Team Licence |
  | Enrollments | they're an Instructor |
  | Discussion Questions | they're an Instructor |
  | Open Refund Requests | they're a Platform Admin |
  | Discussion Replies | always |

  - A hidden switch keeps its default.
  - Each switch saves when flipped, optimistically, through a Cadence action that parses its input with zod. A failed save shows a toast.
  - There's no mute-all.
- **A gear icon** in the Notification Feed popover header links to the card.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Signing up, changing your name, a Platform Admin editing a user, and seeding all sync the user to Knock
- [ ] Sync writes the defaults only for users with no preference set; an existing set is left alone
- [ ] The backfill script syncs every existing user
- [ ] Changing your avatar shows in Notifications you sent earlier
- [ ] The Notifications card shows exactly the switches that fit what the person is or has
- [ ] Flipping a switch saves at once and leaves every other preference unchanged; a failed save shows a toast
- [ ] Muting a category stops new Notifications of that category reaching the feed (for example, mute Discussion Replies and reply to that person's question)
- [ ] The popover's gear links to the card
- [ ] A failed sync is logged and never fails signup or settings
- [ ] vitest covers defaults-only-if-none, merge-on-change and switch visibility against the fake adapter
- [ ] `npm run typecheck` and `npm run test` pass
